body: The shared pattern: trading or leveraged money early, survival through the 1992 boom-bust on the bear side, then a pivot to long-held conviction positions bought during pessimism. Each fortune is ultimately dominated by one asset: D-Mart for Damani, which he built, and Titan for Jhunjhunwala, which he bought. The timing (entering about 1985-86 at the start of India's multi-decade re-rating), the network and survivorship are large non-replicable components.

`case_study:shopify-2015-2025` · tickers US-SHOP · confidence: verified

IPO May 2015 at $17 (10:1 split June 2022 -> ~$1.70). Rose ~6,480% to the Nov 2021 peak (~$169-176 split-adj) as the 'arms dealer' to independent merchants; Merchant Solutions (Shopify Payments, Capital, Shipping) overtook subscriptions — take-rate on GMV, not seats. Crash: 2022 bear market + post-COVID e-commerce normalisation + a capex-heavy logistics push (Deliverr bought for $2.1bn in 2022) returned Shopify to losses; stock -87% to $23.63 (Sept 2022). Reset: 10% layoffs July 2022, then May 2023 20% layoffs and sale of logistics/Deliverr to Flexport for a ~13% stake; stock +27% that day. Back to asset-light: positive operating income for 9+ quarters, FCF margins mid-teens+ [unverified]. New all-time high in late Oct 2025 (surpassing 2021; C$253 on TSX); 2025 was described as its best year. Split: 2015-21 mostly multiple on fast revenue; 2023-25 mostly margins/FCF growth. EARLY SIGNAL visible 2016-18: Payments attach rate rising, Plus enterprise merchants, app-ecosystem revenue — platform economics; in 2023 the signal was management abandoning capex-heavy logistics. Who caught it: founder Tobi Lütke (controlling shares); Baillie Gifford and other growth funds [unverified]. LESSON: a platform that drifts into capital-intensive operations loses its multiple; reversing that drift is itself a buy signal, and recovery to new highs took ~4 years.

- **Start → end:** ~$1.70 split-adj (IPO $17) → ~$169-176 (Nov 2021); new ATH Oct 2025 (~100x IPO->2021)
- **EPS vs rerating:** 2015-21 multiple-heavy; 2023-25 margin/FCF
- **Max drawdown:** -87% (Nov 2021-Sep 2022)
- **Early signal:** payments attach, Merchant Solutions > subscriptions; 2023 logistics exit
- **Who caught it:** Tobi Lütke; growth funds [unverified]
- **Ended/stalled:** recovered to new highs Oct 2025
- **Lesson:** platforms lose multiple when they go capital-heavy; reversal is the signal

`case_study:amazon-1997-2021-compounding` · tickers US-AMZN · confidence: verified

IPO May 1997 at $18. Splits 2:1 (1998), 3:1 (1999), 2:1 (1999), 20:1 (2022) = 240x: IPO ≈ $0.075 on today's basis. Dot-com peak Dec 1999 ~$107 nominal (~$4.4 adj) -> Sept 2001 ~$5.5 (~$0.28 adj): -94%. July 2021 peak ~$3,770 pre-2022-split (~$188): ~2,500x from IPO; ~670x from the 2001 low [split math mine]. Split: EPS was near-zero/negative for years by design; the driver was operating cash flow and later AWS profits; P/E is not meaningful. EARLY SIGNAL visible 1997-2002: the 1997 shareholder letter ('It's all about the long term', optimise for FCF per share, not GAAP EPS), negative working-capital cycle (paid by customers before paying suppliers), and customer counts compounding; Prime (2005) and AWS (2006) were later hidden segments — AWS was first broken out only in 2015, revealing a highly profitable cloud business. Who caught it: Bill Miller (Legg Mason) bought at the IPO, re-entered ~$88 pre-split in the late 1990s, and doubled down near ~$6 in 2001 after a -93% fall, reasoning the book business generated FCF with little inventory risk (247wallst); Nick Sleep/Qais Zakaria (Nomad, from ~2005) [unverified]. Ended/stalled: 2021 peak then -56% in 2022 (see case_study:amazon-drawdown). LESSON: the right metric can differ from EPS (FCF/share, unit economics); a founder willing to reinvest at scale and a hidden segment (AWS) can deliver 1,000x+, but only to holders who survive a -94% drawdown.

- **Start → end:** $18 IPO = ~$0.075 split-adj → ~$188 split-adj (Jul 2021) (~2,500x)
- **EPS vs rerating:** FCF/AWS-driven; P/E not meaningful
- **Max drawdown:** -94% (1999-2001)
- **Early signal:** 1997 letter (FCF/share focus), negative working capital, customer growth; AWS disclosure 2015
- **Who caught it:** Bill Miller (doubled down ~$6 in 2001); Nick Sleep/Nomad [unverified]
- **Ended/stalled:** 2021 peak, -56% 2022
- **Lesson:** right metric + founder reinvestment + hidden segment; survive -94%
- **Sources:** [1](https://www.cnbc.com/2018/12/18/dotcom-bubble-amazon-stock-lost-more-than-90percent-long-term-investors-still-got-rich.html) · [2](https://www.irishtimes.com/business/personal-finance/amazon-s-wild-ride-offers-lessons-for-investors-1.3099248) · [3](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/01/by-2001-his-amazon-shares-had-fallen-93-and-wall-street-was-predicting-the-company-would-go-bankrupt-bill-miller-didnt-care-he-doubled-down-at-6-a-share-two-decades-later-he-had-more-amazon-sto/) · [4](https://www.fool.com/investing/2017/03/22/how-much-money-would-i-have-if-i-had-invested-at-a.aspx)
